summary: Two disks of different sizes on one AHCI controller, both in /proc/disk with their ports and sizes, both with nodes, a partition of each mounted and written, and the second disk's file found on the second disk by the host; the program is tests/cases/machine/disks_scenario.c

cases.behavior: a 64 MiB KRFFS disk on port 0 and a 20 MiB FAT32 disk on port 1 of one AHCI controller are disks 0 and 1, listed in /proc/disk with their ports and sizes and with their nodes, a partition of each mounts and takes a write that reads back, and the write through /dev/disk1p1 is on the second disk

execution.cleanup: libetude-case ends the machine and removes the disks' copies, which it keeps after a failure

steps.does: boot the test image with both disks on the AHCI controller and rach2.diskdiag, run disksprobe at the debug shell: /proc/disk and the nodes of both disks, the KRFFS partition of disk 0 and the FAT32 partition of disk 1 each mounted, written, read back and unmounted; read the kernel's record of each disk, and end the machine with QMP's quit
read one.txt off the FAT32 volume of the second disk's copy with mtype

assertions.checks: disksprobe's line says DISKSPROBE OK, never DISKSPROBE FAIL: /proc/disk lists disk 0 on AHCI port 0 and disk 1 on port 1 with 40960 sectors, disk 0 the larger and no third disk; both disks and their first partitions have nodes, and no absent partition or disk has one; disk 0's KRFFS partition and disk 1's FAT32 partition each mount, take a file that reads back and unmount
the kernel says disk: disk0: ahci 0: 131072 sectors, so the disk on port 0 is disk 0 at its size
the kernel says disk: disk1: ahci 1: 40960 sectors, so the disk on port 1 is disk 1 at its size
mtype reads one.txt off the FAT32 volume at sector 2048 of the second disk's copy, and it says 'disk one says hello', so the write through /dev/disk1p1 reached the disk on port 1

progress.means: a step of the manifest has ended

native.reason: the case needs two disks of its own sizes and tables on ports 0 and 1 of one AHCI controller, a partition of each written, which the Lenovo's one disk cannot give without a raw write
